literal: Poverty called a sinner, next life and this life without, will come.
translation: The wretched sinner called poverty comes, depriving a person of the blessings of both this life and the next.
modern: வறுமை என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஒரு பாவி, ஒருவருக்கு இப்பிறப்பின் இன்பத்தையும் மறுபிறப்பின் இன்பத்தையும் இல்லாமல் செய்து வந்து சேரும்.
explanation: In this couplet, poverty is personified as a wretched sinner ('பாவி'). The author explains that when poverty comes, it completely strips a person of the joys and virtues of both this present life ('இம்மை') and the next life ('மறுமை'). In this world, a poor person lacks the means to live with dignity and comfort, and because they cannot afford to perform acts of charity, they are also deprived of merit for the next world. Thus, poverty is depicted as an all-consuming affliction that ruins a person's existence across both realms.
